title: IT vendor check-in
transcript:
Andre Dubois: Okay, let's get started. Thanks for making time over lunch. Agenda is short: the core vendor's maintenance window next month, the OnlineBanking API throttling issue, the data extract change Amy raised, and then action items. Hector, you've been closest to the vendor, so start us off.
Hector Salas: Sure. The vendor confirmed the CoreBanking patch window for Saturday October 17, starting at 9:00 PM ET and running until roughly 3:00 AM Sunday. They're calling it a quarterly release, with a database patch and a change to the nightly batch scheduler. They said member-facing downtime should be about two hours, but they won't commit to that in writing.
Andre Dubois: That's the part I don't love. CoreBanking is vendor hosted, so we can't see inside the window. Since OnlineBanking depends on it, if the core is down our members see errors in the app even if MemberSSO is fine.
Shannon Sheppard: Right, and last quarter the app showed a generic error page for the whole window. I'd like to put up a proper maintenance banner and have OnlineBanking fail gracefully instead. I can have a static status page ready by the 14th.
Andre Dubois: Good. Does that need a change to MemberSSO?
Shannon Sheppard: No. Login still works, it's only the balance and transaction calls that fail. I'll have the app check a health endpoint for CoreBanking and show the banner when it's unavailable. Small change, but it needs a test pass in staging.
Hector Salas: One more thing on the window. The scheduler change affects when the nightly batch kicks off. That could shift when ShareRecon runs, and those legacy scripts assume the core batch finishes before midnight.
Amy Cole: Yes, that worries me. ShareRecon reads from the core after posting completes. If the vendor moves the batch later, the scripts could pull a partial ledger and we'd get false variances in the GL reconciliation.
Andre Dubois: Can you tell what the new batch timing is?
Hector Salas: I've asked. They owe us the revised schedule by next Wednesday. I'll chase it if it doesn't arrive.
Amy Cole: Then I'll add a guard to ShareRecon so it checks the batch completion flag before it runs, instead of relying on the clock. I can do that this week and test against the vendor's sandbox.
Andre Dubois: Great, please do. Let's log that as IT-482 so it's tracked. Moving on to the API throttling. Shannon, where are we?
Shannon Sheppard: The vendor introduced a rate limit on the core API, and we've been hitting it during the Friday afternoon peak. We saw about a 4 percent rise in timeouts in the mobile app last Friday. The vendor says our current limit is a default tier and they'll raise it for a fee.
Andre Dubois: What's the fee?
Shannon Sheppard: They quoted an increase to the next tier, roughly $1,800 a month. Before we agree, I want to try caching balance lookups for 30 seconds. My estimate is that it cuts our call volume by a third.
Hector Salas: Caching balances makes me a little nervous. Members will expect to see a deposit right away.
Shannon Sheppard: Agreed, so we'd only cache the account summary view, not the post-transaction screens. Anything after a transfer would bypass the cache.
Andre Dubois: Okay. Decision: we try the caching approach first, and we hold off on the paid tier. If timeouts stay above 2 percent after two Fridays, we revisit the upgrade. Shannon, you own that, and please share the before and after numbers.
Shannon Sheppard: Will do. I'll deploy to production the week of October 5 behind a feature flag so we can switch it off quickly.
Andre Dubois: Good. Amy, you had the data extract item.
Amy Cole: Yes. The vendor is retiring the old flat file export at the end of the year and moving to a new API-based extract. Our reporting pipeline and a few of the Compliance feeds consume that flat file today. I did a quick inventory and found five downstream jobs that depend on it.
Andre Dubois: Five, that's more than I expected. Are any tied to BSAWatch?
Amy Cole: One is. BSAWatch pulls through ACHHub and CoreBanking, and there's a secondary nightly file that Compliance uses for reconciliation of alerts. I'll talk to Monica Feld on the Compliance side before we change anything.
Hector Salas: The vendor offered a technical session on the new extract. I can get that scheduled in the next two weeks.
Andre Dubois: Please. Amy, can you put together a migration plan, with each job, owner, and a target cutover date, by October 23? I'd like to be done with all five by mid-November, so we have buffer before the retirement.
Amy Cole: Yes, I can do that. I'll need Hector's help on credentials for the new API.
Hector Salas: No problem. I'll request a sandbox key this week.
Andre Dubois: Anything else for the vendor before we wrap? Any contract items, support escalations?
Hector Salas: Just one. Our support case about the intermittent slow responses on the core is still open, and they asked for logs again. I'll send what we have today and ask for an escalation to their tier two team.
Andre Dubois: Good. Let me recap action items. Hector: get the revised batch schedule by next Wednesday, send logs on the slow response case today, schedule the extract session, and request the sandbox key. Shannon: maintenance banner and health check ready in staging by October 14, and the balance caching rollout the week of October 5 with metrics afterward. Amy: ShareRecon batch completion guard under IT-482 this week, and the extract migration plan by October 23. I'll update the change calendar and tell Member Services about the October 17 window so they can prepare the floor.
Shannon Sheppard: Sounds right to me.
Amy Cole: Same here.
Hector Salas: All good. Thanks, everyone.
Andre Dubois: Thanks, all. We'll reconvene at the next check-in in two weeks.
